scenes.title: s04-flow-foundation
scenes.narration: This is the whole workflow on one page. Blue and grey boxes are steps, yellow ones are checks and skips, red is where things stop or get fixed, orange is a fail, and green is a pass or done. Building the foundation happens once. Checking it happens every time: each campaign starts by verifying that nothing has drifted. If something has, the campaign stops. The subagents testing a story never patch the foundation themselves.

scenes.title: One coordinator hands the work to fresh subagents
scenes.narration: Once the foundation is healthy, a campaign can start. The command you run is the coordinator. It never tests anything itself. It picks the next story, hands the work to fresh subagents one story at a time, and at the end checks their evidence for itself. Each subagent starts with a clean context, so a mistake one subagent made cannot quietly shape the next one's thinking. Depending on the size of the story, one subagent may cover more than one of these jobs.

scenes.title: Four steps finish before any evidence is spent
scenes.narration: Phase one prepares the tests in four steps: analyze, live discovery, author, and preflight. No final evidence is produced until all four are done.

scenes.title: s08-flow-analyze
scenes.narration: Analysis reads each acceptance criterion and lists every separate thing the user should see. Take a criterion that says saving a patient shows a success message and the new record. That is two things, so each one is checked on its own. The result is a requirements checklist, so nothing in the story gets missed.

scenes.title: s09-flow-discovery
scenes.narration: Discovery then opens the running app and learns the real controls, labels and routes. Source code can help with setup, but only the running app shows what the user sees. The facts it records are what the tests are written from.

scenes.title: s10-flow-author
scenes.narration: Just before authoring, there is one check. Does a criterion have two reasonable interpretations that would give different results, with nothing in the story or the live app to settle it? Only then does it stop and ask you one short question. Otherwise it records its assumption and carries on. Then the author writes the Playwright scenarios. Each one states its data, its user, the visible outcome, and the criterion it proves.

scenes.title: s11-flow-preflight
scenes.narration: Preflight checks that the tests really match the story before any time is spent on evidence. If it fails, only the spec is fixed, and preflight runs again. When it passes, the story analysis and the tests are frozen: locked, so nothing can change them while the evidence runs.

scenes.title: Evidence is produced fresh, then judged against the story
scenes.narration: Phase two runs in four steps. First, it confirms the tests are exactly the ones that passed preflight. Then it runs them against a clean environment and records everything. It generates the report and checks the evidence is fresh. Finally, it reviews the result against the story.

scenes.title: A broken test is fixed, not reported
scenes.narration: Every run ends one of two ways. Either it tells you something about the product: pass, fail or skipped, with the evidence kept. A fail means the tool did its job and found a gap for you to fix. A skip means that part could not be checked in the browser: a required precondition could not be met, or it is a rule only the backend can see, which belongs in a backend test. Or the test itself broke. That is a technical fault. It is rechecked, fixed, and run again with fresh evidence.

scenes.title: s14-flow-review
scenes.narration: The review then checks whether the evidence really proves each claim. If it does, the final handoff is written, and the coordinator checks that file and the raw results itself.

scenes.title: s15-flow-teardown
scenes.narration: Finally, teardown removes only what this campaign created, and restores the shared development stack. If it cannot be sure what it owns, it stops rather than guessing.

scenes.title: Most failures go to one of four places
scenes.narration: Most failures go to one of four places. A test problem, stale evidence or weak proof goes back to preflight. A faulty foundation goes back to Phase 0. A genuine ambiguity comes to you as one short question. And an unreachable app, or a teardown that cannot identify its own resources, stops the campaign.

scenes.title: A wrong foundation fix is worse than a skip.
scenes.narration: Foundation repairs get extra checks. When a subagent finds that a small foundation change would unblock a real outcome, it reports the gap instead of making the change. The coordinator sends one subagent to fix it, and a different one to check the fix against the app's real code. A wrong fix can make a test pass when it should not, and a false pass is worse than an honest skip. After two attempts, the decision comes to you.
